d: Kingdom University is seeking a faculty member in Electrical Engineering and Physics for the College of Engineering. You will teach the introduction to engineering, digital design, and university physics with its laboratory component. We are looking for a candidate equally comfortable in a physics lab and an electronics lab. Classes at Kingdom University are built on active learning: students work through problems, discuss and present, and lecturing is only part of each session. Faculty also advise students, contribute to the life of their department, and maintain their own scholarship.
q: Required: PhD in Electrical Engineering, or in Physics with an engineering background. A Master's degree with substantial university teaching experience will also be considered.
Fluency in English and the demonstrated ability to teach effectively in it - all instruction at Kingdom University is delivered in English.
A degree in the relevant field from an accredited university: a doctorate for appointment at Assistant Professor and above, or a Master's degree for appointment at Lecturer.
University-level teaching experience, preferably at the undergraduate level.
Preferred: Laboratory teaching experience and the ability to teach both engineering and physics
r: Teach foundational engineering and physics courses, including laboratory sessions, in the College of Engineering.
Design and supervise laboratory work in both physics and electronics.
Advise students and support their progress through the engineering curriculum.
Contribute to departmental activities and maintain an active program of scholarship.
Teaching assignments draw on the following courses, among others:
Introduction to Engineering • Signals and Systems I
Digital Design Fundamentals • Signals and Systems II
University Physics I: Mechanics, with Laboratory I • Fundamentals of Electromagnetics
University Physics II: Electricity and Magnetism, with Laboratory II • Random Signal Analysis
University Physics III • Hardware Design Languages and Programmable Logic
Circuits I • Properties of Electronic Materials

d: To oversee dnata handling, warehouse and ramp performance, ULD and palletised operations, bulk-loading activity, and compliance with all regulatory, safety, and OEM requirements. The manager ensures operational excellence as flydubai’s cargo operations continue to grow in scale and complexity.
q: Minimum 8 years of experience in cargo operations, freight handling, aviation ground operations Experience in managing large operational teams in cargo, aviation, or ground handling environments

Advanced Cargo & Dangerous Goods courses (Cargo Knowledge, Documentation, Special Load Handling, DGR Cat 6 or CBTA equivalent) Dangerous Goods Regulations (IATA CBTA 7.3A or UAE GCAA FIT4.1D) Safety Management Systems Certification Aviation Security Certification Special Cargo Products Certification
Cargo EDI license desirable Weight & Balance license desirable

Reads and complies with the ISR policies of the Company and diligently reports any weakness or incidents to the respective Line Manager or the Information Security team. Completes all required ISR awareness sessions and follows associated guidelines in the day-to-day business operations.
r: Identify operational objectives and implement approved strategies, policies, and procedures to ensure safe, efficient, and revenue-optimised cargo operations across all aircraft types and operational locations.
Ensures compliance with Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) across all cargo operations, maintaining consistency and accuracy.

Manages and facilitates investigations of accidents, incidents, service failures, irregularities, and customer complaints, ensuring root-cause identification and implementation of corrective and preventive actions.
Prepares and monitors Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Safety Performance Targets in compliance with UAE GCAA standards, covering both bulk and ULD-based operations.
Oversees day-to-day cargo operations at DXB and DWC, ensuring consistent handling standards, and service quality with dnata and other ground handling partners.
Identifies, evaluates and recommends short, medium, and long-term infrastructure, automation, and resource requirements to support current and future cargo operations.
Liaises with dnata and other third-party service providers at DWC to ensure service delivery, SLA compliance, and operational readiness for all aircraft types.
Supports cargo product development, including system automation and the launch cargo products (pharma, express, automotive, oversized cargo, etc.).
Takes ownership of all cargo-related documentation within the Ground Handling Manual (GHM) and ensures timely updates, regulatory alignment, and internal approvals.
Manages cargo safety, security, and risk frameworks, in coordination with Safety & Security, ensuring proper documentation, implementation, and compliance across the operation.
Liaises with government authorities (Customs, Health, Police, and other regulators) at DXB and DWC to ensure the smooth movement of cargo, courier, and mail.

Ensures all ground handling contracts include the required scope of services for both bulk and palletised operations, covering acceptance, ULD handling, warehouse activities, ramp processes, and service standards.

Manage end-to-end project delivery, maintaining quality systems and supporting senior leaders to achieve programme milestones.
